Record.Get is optimized for retrieving a single record based on primary key values.
Record.Find('-') and Record.Find('+') use self-tuning TOP X calls and are best for reading when you might not need all records.
Record.FindSet is optimized for reading the complete set of records in specified filters and ranges.
Each CalcFields or CalcSums call requires a separate SQL statement unless the result is cached from a recent identical calculation.
SetAutoCalcFields method optimizes performance by calculating FlowFields during record retrieval instead of in separate calls.
Using FindSet with var parameter and direct Modify or Delete avoids extra SQL statements compared to copying records.
ModifyAll and DeleteAll revert to individual SQL calls if triggers, event subscribers, security filtering, Media fields, or companion tables exist.
Business Central automatically buffers inserts to send them to SQL Server at one time, reducing server calls and improving performance.
Bulk inserts improve scalability by delaying actual insert until last moment, reducing table lock time especially for SIFT indexes.
Records are sent to SQL Server when COMMIT is called, MODIFY or DELETE is called, or FIND or CALC methods are called.
Bulk inserts are not used if code uses return value from INSERT call or if table contains BLOB fields or AutoIncrement properties.
Disable bulk inserts by setting BufferedInsertEnabled parameter to FALSE in CustomSettings.config file for troubleshooting.
Server data cache is shared by all users connected to same server instance.
GET, FIND, FINDSET, FINDLAST, COUNT, ISEMPTY, and CALCFIELDS methods use cache system.
Global cache is for all users; private cache is per user per company in transactional scope.
Default data cache size is 9 approximating 500 MB; increasing by one doubles the cache size.
Query objects do not use the cache system.
Query is an object used to specify set of data to read from Business Central database, supporting single or multiple tables with joins and totaling.
Sub-query is automatically added to SQL statement for each FlowField in query to retrieve all data in one request.
FlowFields cannot be used on virtual tables in queries because they cannot be automatically converted to SQL statements.
Covering index contains all output fields required by operation and greatly improves performance by retrieving only index data.
SIFT index supports queries with aggregated columns using Sum, Count, or Average methods when totals are part of key fields.
Query result sets are not guaranteed to be dynamic, unlike record result sets which are always dynamic.
SQL Server query optimizer can be overridden with query hints to enforce specific execution plans for SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE statements.
SQL optimization covers compatibility level, data access, table keys, bulk inserts, and query hints

Select Environments > Recently deleted environments, choose environment, optionally modify pending update, then select Recover and confirm.
Early access preview environments deleted due to failed update cannot be recovered; normal deletions recoverable until new build release.
Only internal administrators can initiate and accept environment transfers; delegated admins cannot use this feature.
Transfer must be accepted on destination tenant within 8 hours of creation on source tenant.
On source tenant, select Environments > Environment Transfers, select Transfer Environments, choose environments, enter destination tenant ID, set transfer date/time.
On destination tenant, select Environments > Environment Transfers > Receive Environments, enter source tenant ID, select environments to accept, confirm.
Linked Power Platform environments cannot transfer; must unlink before creating transfer on source tenant.
Early access preview environments can only transfer to destination tenants with Partner Sandbox license.
Renaming changes environment URL; can impact bookmarks, deep links, integrations, mobile apps, and external services.
Environment name limited to 30 characters, must start with letter, contain only letters numbers hyphens underscores; cannot be reserved name like admin or api.
Renaming requires environment restart; recommended during times when no users are active in Business Central.
Select Environments, choose environment, select Rename, enter new name, confirm intent to rename.
Name must be unique within same application family in tenant; environment state changes to Preparing | Rename Scheduled then Active.
Old environment name becomes inaccessible immediately; rename operation logged on Operations page.
Affected areas include web client URLs, deep links to pages, Outlook Excel Power BI add-ins, external integrations, mobile apps, browser cache.
Create Microsoft Entra group, select Environments, choose environment, select Define under Security Group, search and select group, select Save.
Assigning Microsoft Entra group restricts access to direct and indirect group members; internal administrators bypass restriction.
Partner access setting controls delegated administrator and multitenant app access; up to 10 Microsoft Entra tenants per environment allowlisted.
Essentials users can only open companies set to Essentials experience; Premium users access any company but cannot use Premium features in Essentials companies.
Select Environments, choose environment, select Modify for Partner access, toggle Allow partner access on or off, select Save.
By default environments allow all partner access; administrators should restrict to current partners to prevent future auto-access.
Enable Microsoft 365 license access by selecting Environments, choosing environment, selecting Modify for Microsoft 365 licenses setting, toggling on, selecting Save.
Business Central environments contain Microsoft and non-Microsoft apps that work together to provide business features across industries.
Apps can be installed as Global Apps, Per-Tenant Extensions, or DEV extensions with different management capabilities.
New global apps must be installed from Microsoft Marketplace, not directly from admin center, though updates can be installed from admin center.
When app updates introduce dependencies, admin center shows Action Required and lists which apps need updating or installing.
Per-tenant extensions can be scheduled for immediate install, next update window, or next minor/major update with configurable sync mode.
Uninstalling apps may delete application data, which can only be recovered via point-in-time restore unless exported first.
Preview versions of marketplace apps can only install in sandbox environments using a PreviewKey URL, never in production.
Expense Agent, Payables Agent, Sales Order Agent, and AI development toolkit use consumption-based billing charged per use via Copilot Credits.
Expense Agent and AI development toolkit are in preview; Payables Agent and Sales Order Agent are generally available as of November 2026.
Expense Agent costs 25 Copilot Credits per receipt processing and 15 Credits per approval policy check per category.
Sales Order Agent costs 2 Credits per email analysis, 2-5 Credits per attachment processing, and 5 Credits per availability check or order creation.
Payables Agent costs 50 Copilot Credits to process each invoice and 5 Credits per invoice line.
Purchase Copilot Credit packs through Microsoft 365 admin center or Partner Center for prepaid capacity billing.
Allocate Copilot Credit capacity to specific Power Platform environments through Power Platform admin center to control consumption limits.
AI capability becomes unavailable when quota is depleted; expenses without receipts and those without enabled approval policies incur no cost.
Sessions page in admin center shows active sessions on each environment and allows canceling selected sessions.
Canceling sessions unblocks work when, for example, a long-running report locks data preventing other tasks.
Environment restart is available only when environment status is Active.
All users must sign out before restarting an environment to prevent data issues.
Admin center sends email notifications when major updates available, environment updates succeed or fail, or extensions need compatibility changes.
At least one administrator email must be registered as notification recipient to ensure awareness of events requiring action.
Up to 100 notification recipients can be added; use distribution lists to support more recipients.
Email notifications are being replaced by Microsoft 365 Message Center; over time emails will be a subset of Message Center posts.
Application Insights telemetry includes most complete list of environment lifecycle events for automation and reporting.
If app incompatibility blocks updates, Microsoft sends 10 weeks of emails, then 6 weeks in-product notifications, then force-uninstall after 4-5 months.
Admin center telemetry tab shows top-level AL events and errors from telemetry stack for troubleshooting.
Filter telemetry by selecting environment, timestamp, time window, and query category, then search.
Application Insights sends richer telemetry for better troubleshooting than admin center telemetry tab alone.
Application Insights is Azure service that gathers and analyzes telemetry data for environments.
Update window defines daily hours in specified time zone when environment can be updated by Microsoft.
Default update window is 8:00 PM to 6:00 AM local time; minimum window duration is six hours.
Updates failing to complete before window end are automatically canceled and rescheduled seven days later.
Admins can schedule updates to any version higher than current within environment's major version.
During preview periods, sandbox environments can schedule updates to preview versions without email notifications.
Planned versions allow scheduling before Microsoft releases; update scheduled automatically within seven days after version availability.
Running updates can be manually canceled, restoring environment to pre-update state; cancellation may take over an hour.
Updates cannot be canceled during Enforced Update Period for source version.
Internal administrators need Dynamics 365 Business Central Administrator role minimum for tenant administration.
Delegated administrators are partner company employees with GDAP relationship; Dynamics 365 Business Central Administrator role recommended.
Internal administrators have read-only access to all Business Central areas even after subscription cancellation.
Internal administrators need Business Central license to set up integrations or perform tasks beyond user management and data export.
License Administrator role required in Microsoft 365 admin center to manage subscription and assign licenses.
User Administrator role required in Microsoft 365 admin center to add or remove users from tenant.
Partners can log in as delegated administrator to set up and troubleshoot customer environments.
Switching partners requires removing reseller relationship, disabling delegated admin, clearing partner settings, and adding new partner.
Users must sign up with a work or school account tied to a Microsoft 365 subscription and Microsoft Entra tenant.
Each Microsoft Entra tenant receives automatic environments upon licensing; each environment ties to a country and localization.
Environments can contain multiple companies, each representing a legal entity with separate accounting requirements.
Organizations can transfer environments between Microsoft Entra tenants if structure changes.
Users with same license access all companies in all environments their Microsoft Entra tenant owns; permissions controlled within Business Central.
Users from different Microsoft Entra tenants cannot access the same environment.
Partners can create test environments for testing or pre-sales demonstrations.
Test environments based on free 30-day trials require CSP access in Partner Center.
In Partner Center, create new test customer with test domain like contoso.onmicrosoft.com.
Subscribe to Dynamics 365 Business Central Premium Trial providing 25 licenses for 30 days.
Create test user and assign 1 Premium license; may take 10 minutes for licenses to display.
Environment created automatically when first logging in with user credentials to Business Central.
Windows Performance Monitor collects and displays performance data from counters and trace events in real time or logs.
Event Viewer on Windows displays Business Central Server events in Applications and Services Logs.
Logman.exe command-line tool manages event trace sessions and performance logs on Windows.
Get-WinEvent PowerShell cmdlet retrieves Business Central Server instance events from Windows event logs.
PerfView analyzes performance issues related to Event Tracing for Windows data.
Microsoft TraceEvent Library provides classes for controlling ETW providers and parsing events.
Organizations can sign up for a free Business Central trial to explore the experience.
A 30-day trial is available without sample data, allowing users to add their own business data for evaluation.
Users can extend the trial period if 30 days are not enough to decide on a subscription.
Viral trials do not expire unless the prospect switches to the 30-day trial, provided users access Business Central frequently.
If an organization stops using Business Central, the administrator must remove the subscription in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
All customers, including trial organizations, can use sandbox environments for practicing without affecting production.
Strongly not recommended to use a free trial to run your business; contact a reselling partner to migrate data.
Long-running SQL queries meeting or exceeding SqlLongRunningThreshold are logged as warnings in Event Viewer.
Default SqlLongRunningThreshold is 750 milliseconds; can be changed without restarting server instance.
AL call stack in event log shows which AL method generated slow-running SQL queries from explicit AL code.
Queries from GetPage calls or empty triggers may not include AL call stack due to no explicit AL code execution.
Generated SQL statement appears in Statement field; AL call stack shown in AL CallStack field of event log entry.
SQL Server Query Store captures query history, compilation metrics, and runtime statistics aggregated over time intervals.
Query Store available in SQL Server starting with version 2016 and Azure SQL Database.
Query Store helps identify queries with longest execution time, biggest IO reads, and other performance metrics.
Query Store retains history of aggregated metrics, not individual query execution logs.
SmartSQL optimization performs all FlowField calculations on a page using a single SQL query, reducing network roundtrips to the database.
SmartSQL adds an OUTER APPLY clause to the SQL statement for each FlowField in the table.
To isolate FlowField query performance issues, run the Business Central administration tool and select the Disable SmartSQL checkbox in the Database section.
When SmartSQL is disabled, each FlowField calculation is performed as a separate SQL statement instead of being combined.
After identifying a slow FlowField subquery, create an index or enable the MaintainSIFTIndex property of the key to improve performance.
SmartSQL queries are not cached, which can amplify performance issues and disabling it does not require page customization or field visibility changes.
SAML2 token errors occur when the security token lifetime from Microsoft Entra ID has exceeded its default limit of 1 hour.
Users experience a connection lost error message when the SAML2 token validity period ends.
The server includes a configuration setting called ExtendedSecurityTokenLifetime that adds time to the security token lifetime.
To resolve token expiration issues, increase the ExtendedSecurityTokenLifetime setting on the Business Central server.
The Windows client times out after 9 or more hours of continuous connection, causing an ID4148 error that cannot be changed.
Resolve Windows client timeout by closing and reopening the client application.
The Business Central server requires Named Pipes and TCP/IP protocols to be enabled in SQL Server Configuration Manager for proper database connectivity.
In SQL Server Configuration Manager, expand the SQL Server Network Configuration node and select Protocols for MSSQLSERVER to verify or enable Named Pipes and TCP/IP.
If a protocol is disabled, right-click it and select Enable, then restart the Business Central server.
Windows Firewall must explicitly allow the SQL Server executable file sqlservr.exe as an exception to permit connections.
In Windows Firewall exceptions, add the SQL Server executable at C:\Program Files\Microsoft SQL Server\MSSQL*\MSSQL\Binn\sqlservr.exe.
When using a named database instance with the server and SQL Server on separate computers, the SQL Browser Service must be running on the SQL Server.
ClientServicesIdleClientTimeout on server controls inactive connection timeout; defaults to MaxValue (no limit).
SessionTimeout on web server controls inactive session timeout; defaults to 20 minutes.
Session closes based on whichever timeout setting has the shortest period between server and web server.
ClientServicesReconnectPeriod applies to Business Central 2022 version 20 and earlier only.
In Business Central 2023 and later, sessions terminate instantly when client loses connection; reconnection isn't supported.
Use Set-NAVServerConfiguration and Set-NAVWebServerInstanceConfiguration PowerShell commands to modify timeout settings.
If active session exists during timeout, server aborts current call stack, rolls back uncommitted transactions, and closes session.
Excel add-in update rolled out starting July 2022 to secure connection between add-in and Business Central.
Update affects on-premises, hosted, and private cloud deployments; Business Central online customers not affected.
After update users cannot sign in to add-in if redirect URI is not changed in Microsoft Entra app registration.
Sign in to Azure portal and go to Microsoft Entra ID App Registrations.
Select the Excel add-in app registration and go to Manifest.
Change redirect URI type from Web to Spa in the manifest.
Changes can be made at any time; existing add-in works with the new configuration.
Generally available. Two major releases occur every April and October.
Preview period starts one month before major release, typically March and September. Partner Sandbox tenants access early access preview alongside the entire update period.
Update period begins when major version is generally available, around first workday of April and October. New environments created on new major version.
Update period lasts five calendar months, ending early September for April releases and early March for October releases. Administrators can reschedule updates within this period.
Grace period lasts one month following the update period. During grace period, admins cannot reschedule updates to later dates, only to earlier dates or different major versions.
Enforced update period begins when grace period ends. Extensions causing update failures may be automatically uninstalled so updates succeed.
Cannot restore an environment to a version in its Grace or Enforced update period after updating to a later version succeeds.
Minor updates release monthly except April and October, containing critical improvements and regulatory updates. Generally available at start of each calendar month.
Server events are collected in Debug logs under Applications and Services Logs for DynamicsNAV Server and Common.
Debug logs are disabled by default and may be hidden in Event Viewer.
Open Event Viewer on the computer running the server.
Navigate to Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > DynamicsNAV > Server or Common.
Show Analytic and Debug Logs from the View menu if Debug log is not visible.
Select Debug log and choose Enable Log from the Actions menu.
Default log size is 1028 KB; increase if needed based on event volume.
Table partitioning divides large tables across filegroups for faster maintenance, improved queries, and better performance via partition elimination.
Partitioning field must be included in the table's primary key in AL code; partitioning is configured in SQL Server after table publication.
Primary key fields cannot be added after an extension publishes to production; partitioning is limited to new extensions or existing ones with partitioning fields already in primary keys.
Compression reduces table size and improves I/O-intensive workload performance; CompressionType property lets you set Row, Page, or Unspecified compression.
In Business Central online, tables are compressed using Page compression by default.
Partitioning and compression can be combined for flexible data archiving on historical partitions without CPU overhead on active parts.
Version format is major.minor.build.revision, example 27.1.23456.0 for application version.
Major version 28 represents 2026 release wave 1 April 2026 and forward.
Major version 27 represents 2025 release wave 2 October 2025 and forward.
Major version 26 represents 2025 release wave 1 April 2025 and forward.
Minor number indicates monthly update; build is five digit number; revision stays 0 unless hotfix applied.
Online admin center uses only major.minor version for managing environment updates, not full build numbers.
Version numbers identify both cloud and on-premises deployments including Docker container versions.
Public preview. Business Central online version 29.1 or later with Mirroring to Fabric extension required.
Available for Business Central online only, not on-premises or Docker environments.
Workspace assigned to active Fabric capacity or supported Fabric trial. Paused capacity stops replication.
MS Fabric Mirroring - Admin to configure, Activate to manage packages, Read for synchronization monitoring.
Mirroring copies initial data then syncs changes. Use when API refreshes are slow or combining data from multiple systems.
Up to 1,000 selected tables across manual selections and packages. FlowFields and BLOB fields excluded.
Cannot filter records, specify time periods, choose individual fields, or configure different intervals per table.
No Business Central fee for mirroring. Fabric doesn't charge replication compute but charges for storage beyond free allowance and queries.
